```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE)
library(WorldFloraFast)
```

WorldFloraFast matches plant names against the taxonomic backbone of the
[World Flora Online](https://www.worldfloraonline.org) (WFO): it corrects spelling
mistakes, recognises synonyms and returns the currently accepted names. It is a faster,
refactored derivative of the WorldFlora package (Kindt 2020), with the same functions and
arguments.

## 1. Obtain the backbone

The backbone (`classification.csv`, about 1.6 million names) is published on Zenodo.
`WFO.download()` downloads the latest release, verifies its checksum, remembers where it
is and loads it as `WFO.data`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
WFO.download(save.dir = "wfo_data")              # first time: about 1 GB
WFO.download(save.dir = "wfo_data", update = TRUE)  # later: newer release?
WFO.remember()                                   # new session: load WFO.data again
WFO.data <- WFO.read("wfo_data", core.only = TRUE)  # or read fewer columns
```

This vignette uses `WFO.example2026`, a small extract of the WFO Plant List 2026-06 that is
included in the package.

```{r}
data(WFO.example2026)
head(WFO.example2026[, c("taxonID", "scientificName", "taxonRank", "taxonomicStatus")])
```

## 2. Prepare names that include authors

Names in field data or literature often include authors. `WFO.prepare()` separates them;
the `Authorship` column then helps to choose between homonyms.

```{r}
x <- c("Faidherbia albida (Delile) A.Chev.", "Acacia albida Delile", "Pygeum afric Hook. f.")
prep <- WFO.prepare(x, verbose = FALSE)
prep[, c("spec.full", "spec.name", "Authorship")]
```

## 3. Match the names

```{r}
m <- WFO.match(prep, WFO.data = WFO.example2026, verbose = FALSE)
m[, c("spec.name", "Subseq", "Fuzzy", "scientificName", "scientificNameAuthorship", "Old.name", "Old.author")]
```

* *Faidherbia albida* is matched exactly.
* *Acacia albida* has three homonyms in the WFO: *A. albida* Delile is a synonym of
  *Faidherbia albida*, *A. albida* Lindl. a synonym of *Vachellia tortuosa*, and *A. albida*
  Rojas Acosta is an accepted name. All three are returned, numbered by `Subseq`; synonyms
  are replaced by their accepted names and kept in `Old.name`.
* *Pygeum afric* is incomplete: fuzzy matching finds *Pygeum africanum*, a synonym of
  *Prunus africana*.

Names can also be given as a character vector, or in separate columns `Genus`, `Species`,
`Infraspecific.rank` and `Infraspecific` (exact matching only).

## 4. Keep one match per name

`WFO.one()` keeps one row per submitted name. With the distances between submitted and
matched authors, the homonym *A. albida* Delile is chosen:

```{r}
one <- WFO.one(m, Auth.dist = "Auth.dist", Old.author.dist = "Old.author.dist", verbose = FALSE)
one[, c("spec.name", "Authorship", "scientificName", "Old.name", "One.Reason")]
```

Without authors, `WFO.one()` prefers accepted names, then names that were not synonyms
(here *A. albida* Rojas Acosta), then the smallest `taxonID`; `One.Reason` shows what
decided.

### Fuzzy matching options

`Fuzzy` is the maximum distance (a fraction of the name length, or a number of edits). By
default only the closest candidates are kept (`Fuzzy.min = TRUE`); with
`Fuzzy.min = FALSE`, all candidates within the distance are returned, one row each:

```{r}
all.cand <- WFO.match("Omalanthus populneus", WFO.data = WFO.example2026, Fuzzy.min = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
all.cand[, c("Subseq", "Fuzzy.dist", "scientificName", "taxonomicStatus", "Old.name")]
```

`Fuzzy.dist` is the distance to the name that was matched, which for replaced synonyms is
`Old.name` (here, varieties replaced by their species).

## 5. Names that need more than spelling corrections

By default, `WFO.match()` uses the matching steps of WorldFlora, with three corrections
that can each be switched off: a correctly spelled genus is not replaced by another one
(`Fuzzy.keep.genus`), fuzzy matches must have a similar epithet (`Fuzzy.epithet.check`), and
placeholders such as "indet." or "sp." are not matched (`Fuzzy.skip.placeholder`). When
neither a name nor its first two words are found, it falls back to the genus.
WorldFloraFast offers three optional steps for such names, switched off by default:

* **genus, then epithet** (`Fuzzy.genus`): for truncated or misspelled genera;
* **genus transfer** (`Fuzzy.transfer`): the same epithet in another genus of the family,
  when the backbone shows that species moved from the submitted genus to that genus;
* **strict genus fall-back** (`Fuzzy.one.strict`): the genus only when the first word is an
  accepted genus name, so that local names are not given a scientific name.

```{r}
x <- c("Reinwardtiod cinerum", "Chrysophyllum madagascariensis", "Palma colorada")
default <- WFO.one(WFO.match(x, WFO.data = WFO.example2026, verbose = FALSE), verbose = FALSE)
edge <- WFO.match(x, WFO.data = WFO.example2026, verbose = FALSE,
                  Fuzzy.genus = TRUE, Fuzzy.transfer = TRUE, Fuzzy.one.strict = TRUE)
data.frame(submitted = x, default = default$scientificName,
           optional.steps = ifelse(edge$Matched, edge$scientificName, "(not matched)"))
```

* "Reinwardtiod cinerum" is *Reinwardtiodendron cinereum*: the epithet is found in the
  genus that starts with "Reinwardtiod" (and not in *Reinwardtia*, which is closer by
  spelling).
* For "Chrysophyllum madagascariensis", Sapotaceae contain several species with this
  epithet, but only *Gambeya madagascariensis* belongs to an accepted species (*Gambeya
  boiviniana*) that also has a synonym in *Chrysophyllum* (*Chrysophyllum boivinianum*):
  *Chrysophyllum* species of Madagascar were moved to *Gambeya*.
* "Palma colorada" is a local name. *Palma* Mill. is a synonym of *Phoenix*, so the genus
  fall-back is not used and the name stays unmatched.

Matches found by these steps are flagged and should be checked. Fuzzy matching cannot
recognise every local name: names that are themselves in the backbone (such as the genus
*Guayaba*) are matched, and `agrep()` can find a local name within a longer scientific
name, giving a large `Fuzzy.dist`.

## 6. Explore

```{r}
WFO.synonyms("Gambeya boiviniana", WFO.data = WFO.example2026, verbose = FALSE)
WFO.family("Gambeya boiviniana", WFO.data = WFO.example2026, verbose = FALSE)[, c("Family", "Order", "Node.1")]
WFO.url(edge[1, ])
```

`WFO.browse()` lists the genera of a family, the species of a genus or the infraspecific
taxa of a species.

## 7. Other backbones

Any taxonomic list with identifiers, names, authors and accepted-name identifiers can be
used instead of the WFO:

```{r}
mammals <- data.frame(id = c("M1", "M2"), name = c("Felis catus", "Felis domesticus"),
                      author = c("Linnaeus, 1758", "Erxleben, 1777"), accepted = c("", "M1"))
bb <- new.backbone(mammals, taxonID = "id", scientificName = "name",
                   scientificNameAuthorship = "author", acceptedNameUsageID = "accepted")
WFO.match("Felis domestica", WFO.data = bb, verbose = FALSE)[, c("spec.name", "scientificName", "Old.name")]
```

## Performance

With the WFO Plant List 2026-06 (1.66 million names), matching 50,000 records takes about
5 seconds, and a misspelled name about 0.3 seconds:

* the backbone is indexed once, so exact matches and accepted names are hash lookups;
* each distinct name is fuzzy-matched once (in parallel with `cores = n` on Linux and
  macOS);
* before each `agrep()` search, an exact prefilter discards names that cannot be within
  the allowed number of edits;
* the index is kept for the next call with the same backbone, so that further calls take
  a fraction of a second. Keep the backbone as the data.table returned by `WFO.read()` or
  `WFO.remember()`: a data.frame is copied at each call.

With `Fuzzy.keep.genus`, `Fuzzy.epithet.check` and `Fuzzy.skip.placeholder` set to `FALSE`
(the optional steps are off by default), results are those of WorldFlora 1.14-5 apart from
the corrections listed in `news(package = "WorldFloraFast")`.

## Reference

Kindt, R. (2020). WorldFlora: An R package for exact and fuzzy matching of plant names
against the World Flora Online taxonomic backbone data. *Applications in Plant Sciences*
8(9): e11388. <https://doi.org/10.1002/aps3.11388>
